corrected_value.title: Ongoing Victim Suffering Increases Prejudice: The Case of Secondary Anti-Semitism
corrected_value.title_o: Ongoing Victim Suffering Increases Prejudice: The Case of Secondary Anti-Semitism

decisions.quote:
In the first study, we aimed to replicate Imhoff and
                                                                Banse’s (2009) study and to test the role of latent guilt
                                                                as a potential mediating process.
decisions.location: Study 1, p. 4, lines 205-207 (see also References, p. 20, lines 1193-1196)
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding (target 0) accurately identify Imhoff & Banse (2009), 'Ongoing victim suffering increases prejudice: The case of secondary anti-semitism', Psychological Science, 20, 1443-1447, as the single published original study re-tested across all eight studies (Studies 1, 2, 3a, 3b, 3c, 4a, 4b, and 5) in this file-drawer report. Other cited works provide theoretical background or measurement instruments/paradigms and are not replication targets.

decisions.quote:
In light of a failure to replicate the basic effect, however, the studies
                        shifted to an effort to demonstrate the basic process. We report all studies our lab has con-
                        ducted on the issue. Overall, the data did not provide any evidence for the original effect.
decisions.reason: With the original target resolved to Imhoff & Banse (2009) and the study type confirmed as a replication, the authors state an explicit overall verdict that the replication failed across all eight studies and their internal meta-analysis ('Overall, the data did not provide any evidence for the original effect'; 'In summary, we repeatedly failed to conceptually replicate one of our findings across a relatively large number of studies, with different methodological approaches'). Both shipped and blind codings rightly record 'failed'.

decisions.quote:
Based on the – to the best of our knowledge – only experimental evidence
                        for such an effect (published in Psychological Science in 2009), the present research reports a
                        series of studies originally conducted to better understand the contribution of the different
                        assumed mechanisms. In light of a failure to replicate the basic effect, however, the studies
                        shifted to an effort to demonstrate the basic process.
decisions.reason: The paper collects new experimental data across eight studies using new participant samples to re-test the previously published experimental finding of Imhoff & Banse (2009). Both shipped and blind codings rightly classify the record type as 'replication'.
